context.description: A VERIFY.md with no ensures fails rule R3

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review of packages/opencode/test/task/verify-spec-VF3.spec.ts (4 tests, titles [VF3]); my own bun test run: 4 pass, 0 fail, 32 expect() calls. GIVEN a leaf VERIFY.md with no ensures key: a temp copy of release-notes.spec with the whole ensures block of T1.2 VERIFY.md removed; the test asserts the original had ensures, the edited text has no 'ensures' at all, keeps hint and gates and its front-matter fence, and T1.2 has no child task folder (a leaf). WHEN the spec loads: the real Blend.load. THEN R3: failures equal exactly [{rule R3, path T1.2 VERIFY.md, message "(root): 'ensures' is a required property"}] and no spec is returned. AND the JSON schema lists ensures as required: the committed task-formats/blend/schema/verify.schema.json (title 'VERIFY.md front matter') has top-level required equal to ['ensures'] and an ensures property. The writer noted no JSON Schema validator runs. I judge the step still proven: it states that the schema LISTS ensures as required, which is a structural fact that the assertion reads directly; I checked that the schema root is a draft 2020-12 type object with additionalProperties false and no root $ref or allOf, so the top-level required list is the effective constraint. AND the release-notes and provider-ordering-admin specs load from task-formats/blend with zero failures, a defined spec, at least one task, and an obligation for every task. A control shows the unedited copy loads clean, so the R3 failure comes from the removed ensures only. No gap found.
